Sticky Problem

Game StrategyParity

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)

Game: Break sticks or clear matching lengths until none remain — the player who takes the last piece wins.
How to play: Choose Break or Remove. For Break, click a square to the right of where you want to snap. For Remove, click a stick when you have n sticks of length n. Use Make move to let the computer go first.
Move type
Look for the math

This is American Mathematical Monthly problem 10967 (styled here after Sung Soo Kim’s sticky-bar game). Every position is a count of sticks of each length: write it as a quadruple (k, l, m, n) for lengths 1, 2, 3 and 4.

Two kinds of move

You may break a stick of length at least 2 into two shorter positive lengths, or remove n sticks that each have length n. The player who makes the last move wins — ordinary normal play.

A parity filter

Let r = (k + m) mod 2 and s = (l + n) mod 3. Li Zhou’s solution shows that the P-positions (previous-player wins with perfect play) are exactly those with r = s. The empty board is one of them. The classic start (1, 0, 0, 4) — one singleton and four fours — also satisfies r = s, so the second player can force a win.

Checking the claim

The logic test walks every count tuple with each coordinate at most 5 (1 296 positions). From every P-position every legal move lands in an N-position, and from every N-position some move returns to a P-position — matching the page’s proof outline. The computer’s replies copy the applet’s Play() branches on s − r.

Start from 1 + 4×4 and press Make move so the computer opens. Can you still steal a win if it slips off the P-set?
